pages.quiz:
GENERAL SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: GENERAL SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

2. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. joule (J)
   D. watt (W)

3. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Iron rusting

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Skeletal and Muscular System? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Skeletal and Muscular System.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Skeletal and Muscular System.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Skeletal and Muscular System.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Skeletal and Muscular System.

5. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Producers
   D. Tertiary consumers

6. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

7. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only water vapour

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Ecosystems? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Ecosystems.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on The Ecosystems.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Ecosystems.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Ecosystems.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Detergents ● Soapy and soapless detergents ● Preparations of detergents ● Mode o? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Detergents ● Soapy and soapless detergents ● Preparations of detergents ● Mode o.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Detergents ● Soapy and soapless detergents ● Preparations of detergents ● Mode o.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Detergents ● Soapy and soapless detergents ● Preparations of detergents ● Mode o.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Detergents ● Soapy and soapless detergents ● Preparations of detergents ● Mode o.

10. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

11. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electrostatics? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrostatics.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Electrostatics.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrostatics.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electrostatics.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Genetics ● Meaning of terms and concepts in genetics (Deoxyribon and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Evolution and Biodiversity and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Skeletal and Muscular System and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Carbon and its Oxides and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

2. A — newton (N)

3. B — Ice melting to water

4. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Skeletal and Muscular System.

5. C — Producers

6. C — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

7. C — Glucose and oxygen

8. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Ecosystems.

9. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Detergents ● Soapy and soapless detergents ● Preparations of detergents ● Mode o.

10. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

11. D — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

12. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrostatics.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Evolution and Biodiversity; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Skeletal and Muscular System; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Carbon and its Oxides; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
